text: The crawler mapped a new column positionally instead of recognizing it. The real fix has two parts, in order: stop this from happening again, then repair the data that's already wrong. Skipping either half leaves a real problem behind.

The ETL job trusted column order, which is exactly what broke. Rewrite it to select the expected columns by name instead. Each name resolves against the real header in every file, so a file with sales_channel inserted mid-row and a file without it now produce the identical set of output columns. Position no longer matters at all.

The crawler needs the same correction. Configure its classifier to the native CSV classifier with has-headings recognition enabled, instead of inferring columns purely by sampling. Re-run it, and sales_channel now shows up as its own named column, in its real position, with older files correctly showing it as null.

Fixing the job and crawler stops new damage, but does nothing for partitions already written wrong. Delete the bad curated partitions for the affected date range, reset the job's bookmark so it reprocesses those dates instead of skipping them as already done, rerun the ETL job, then re-run the Lesson 5 COPY to reload the corrected partitions.

Re-run the Finance report for that range. Region values read as real names again, with sensible totals. Spot-check one order against the raw file sampled last lesson, and it genuinely matches. Next: wrapping up everything this project built.
